items.readme:
# Aerial **给国产电视的一块干净桌面。** 参照 tvOS 设计的 Android TV 桌面：没有广告，没有推荐流，只有你的 App、你的壁纸和 Apple TV 航拍屏保。
为小米、TCL 等国产电视而做，开机自动接管，待机也不会被清理。 **中文** · [English](README.en.md) ![Aerial 首页](site/img/home.jpg) | 电视自带的桌面 | 换上 Aerial 之后 | |:---:|:---:| | | |
## 功能 ### 首页

- **时钟**：大号细体时钟压在壁纸上，壁纸底部和左侧自动压暗。往下滚动时，时钟收进状态栏。 - **应用网格**：每行 5 个，聚焦时浮起并显示名字。默认加一圈白色描边，离得远也看得清；在「控制中心 → Aerial 设置」可以改回 tvOS 的原样。 - **图标**：有电视横幅就用横幅；方形图标用自己的底色铺满磁贴；自适应图标拆成两层做视差。 - **全部 App**：小米「应用中心」「高清播放器」「米家」这类没有标准入口的系统 App 也会显示。 - **信号源磁贴**：把 HDMI、AV、电视天线固定到首页，按一下直接切换（控制中心 → 信号源 → 显示在主屏幕）。 - **返回键**：和 tvOS 一样，在网格里按返回回到第一行，在第一行按返回开始屏保。 ### 长按菜单 ![长按菜单](site/img/menu.jpg) 长按 OK 键：**移动**（其他磁贴自动让位）、**从主屏幕隐藏**、**应用信息**、**卸载**。 ### 控制中心 ![控制中心](site/img/control-center.jpg) 按遥控器的菜单键（≡）打开，或在第一行按上键。包括信号源（显示 CEC 设备）、网络、设置，音量和亮度滑块，以及壁纸与屏保、隐藏的 App、Aerial 设置。网络和设置会打开电视自己的面板。 ### 屏保

- **航拍**：114 段 Apple TV 航拍影片，从 Apple 的服务器直接播放，镜头移动时显示地名。左右键切换上一段 / 下一段。 - **照片**：每日精选和你的照片缓慢推移。 - **时钟**：每分钟换一个位置，防止烧屏。 在使用 Android 标准屏保的电视（比如 TCL）上，Aerial 就是系统屏保。小米用自家的屏保，Aerial 会在桌面空闲时抢先启动，挡在小米的广告屏保前面。 ### 壁纸与手机设置

- **壁纸**：必应每日精选（国内直连）、8 组内置渐变，或者你自己的照片。 - **用手机设置**：扫描壁纸面板上的二维码，在手机上传照片、选壁纸、换屏保。页面只在面板打开时开放，地址带随机令牌。 ## 安装 不需要 root，**不卸载、不停用任何系统应用**，一条命令就能还原。 ### 第一步：打开电视的 ADB 调试 电脑和电视连同一个网络。先在电视上找到 IP 地址（一般在「设置 → 网络」或「关于」里），再打开 ADB： | 电视 | 怎么打开 | |---|---| | **小米 / Redmi** | 设置 → 关于 → **产品型号**，连续按确认键，直到提示已进入开发者模式。再到 设置 → 账号与安全，打开 **ADB 调试** 和 **安装未知来源的应用** | | **TCL / 雷鸟** | 设置 → 关于 → **本机信息**，依次按遥控器的 **上、下、左、右**（间隔不超过 1 秒），底部会出现「更多」，在里面打开 **ADB** | | **原生 Android TV / Google TV**、海信等 | 设置 → 设备偏好设置 → 关于 → 连续按 **版本号** 7 次；再到 开发者选项 打开 **USB 调试**（也可能叫「网络调试」或「ADB 调试」） | 电脑第一次连接时，电视会问「允许 USB 调试吗？」，选 **允许** 并勾上「始终允许」。 ### 用 Agent 安装（推荐） 把下面这段交给 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类能在你电脑上运行命令的 Agent，把 `<电视IP>` 换成你的电视 IP： ```text 请帮我把开源电视桌面 Aerial（https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv）安装到我的电视上，并让它成为开机自动启动的桌面。 我的电视 IP 是：<电视IP> 请按这个顺序做： 1. 读一下仓库 README 的「安装」部分和 docs/devices/ 下的机型笔记。 2. 确认电脑上有 adb、curl、python3（没有 adb 也可以，安装脚本会自动下载 Google 的 platform-tools）。 3. 运行 adb connect <电视IP>:5555。连不上就提醒我按 README 在电视上打开 ADB 调试；显示 unauthorized 就提醒我在电视上点「允许」。 4. 运行一键安装： curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | KEEP_ADB=1 TV=<电视IP> bash 如果是 TCL，电视右上角会弹出「多屏互动：正在发起应用推送」，提醒我在电视上选「同意」。 5. 装完后用 adb shell dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus 确认前台是 app.orchard.tv；征得我同意后再 adb reboot 一次，确认开机直接进入 Aerial。 6. 不要卸载或停用任何系统应用，不要删除电视上不是这次安装创建的文件。失败时把命令输出原样给我看，再参考 docs/devices/ 排查。 ``` ### 一行命令（macOS / Linux） ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | KEEP_ADB=1 TV=192.168.1.20 bash ``` 脚本会下载最新版 APK 安装，授予只有 ADB 能给的权限（见下表），预编译让它更流畅，然后接管桌面和屏保、放行开机自启。 - `KEEP_ADB=1`：电视关掉 ADB 调试后（小米待机唤醒时会关），Aerial 立刻重新打开。不需要可以去掉。 - **固件拒绝安装桌面类 App**：在命令最后加 `-s guard`，改装不声明 HOME 的版本。 - **TCL**：TCL 拒绝一切 ADB 安装，脚本会改用电视自带的「多屏互动」推送，你在电视上选一次「同意」即可；没有多屏互动时退回用当贝市场。 还原成原来的桌面： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | TV=192.168.1.20 bash -s restore ``` ### 手动安装 到 [Releases](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/releases/latest) 下载 `aerial-standard.apk`（固件拒绝安装桌面类 App 时用 `aerial-guard.apk`），然后： ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.20:5555 adb install -r aerial-standard.apk adb shell pm grant app.orchard.tv android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS adb shell cmd notification allow_listener app.orchard.tv/app.orchard.tv.guard.RevivalListener adb shell appops set app.orchard.tv SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow adb shell am start -n app.orchard.tv/.MainActivity ``` Aerial 启动后会自己打开桌面守护。屏保、亮度、TCL 自启等完整步骤见 [tools/install.sh](tools/install.sh)。 ## 它怎么接管桌面，又怎么不被杀掉 国产电视大多只认自家桌面，待机时还会清理第三方 App。Aerial 先温和、后强硬： 1. **正常申请**：申请 HOME 角色、设为默认桌面。原生 Android TV 和 Google TV 到这一步就够了。 2. **桌面守护**：固件坚持用自家桌面时（小米、TCL 都是），由一个无障碍服务接管：官方桌面一到前台，就把 Aerial 拉回来。它只看哪个窗口到了前台，不读屏幕内容。 3. **被杀后复活**：小米待机会强制停止所有第三方 App。Aerial 注册了一个通知监听（不读任何通知），系统会在约 0.5 秒内重新绑定它，Aerial 借此复活，并用 `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` 重新打开守护。 4. **开机自启**：开机时系统绑定通知监听，Aerial 随之启动。TCL 的「自启动管理」默认拦截第三方 App，安装脚本会用 `appops` 放行。 5. **ADB 常开**（可选）：小米唤醒后会关掉 ADB 调试，开了 `KEEP_ADB` 后 Aerial 会马上打开它，方便以后升级。 ### ADB 授予的权限 | 权限 | 用途 | |---|---| | `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` | 重新打开被系统关掉的守护；保持 Aerial 为系统屏保；`KEEP_ADB`；写入小米的背光值 | | 通知监听 | 被强制停止或开机后由系统拉起，不读取任何通知 | | 悬浮窗（`SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`） | 开机后从后台打开 Aerial | | 修改系统设置 | 用标准接口调节亮度 | | 定位 | 只用来读取 Wi-Fi 名称 | | TCL `APP_AUTO_START` / `APP_ASSOC_START` | 允许开机自启（只有 TCL 有） | ## 已验证的电视 | 机型 | 系统 | 状态 | 笔记 | |---|---|---|---| | 小米 MiTV-MFTR0 | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 日常使用中 | [笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mftr0.md) | | 小米 MiTV-MFFU0 | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 安装、开机自启已验证 | [笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mffu0.md) | | Redmi X65 2026（MiTV-MFTR0） | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 用户验证：安装、重启后自动进入（[#3](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/3)） | 同 MiTV-MFTR0 | | TCL MT5879 国行 | Android 11 | 日常使用中 | [笔记](docs/devices/tcl-mt5879-cn.md) | | 索尼 XRJ-77A80J 国行（BRAVIA VH2） | Android 10 | 用户验证：安装、开机自启、待机唤醒、屏保（[#16](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/16)） | — | | 索尼 BRAVIA VH1 国行 | Android 12 | 用户验证；亮度改为打开索尼的图像设置（[#2](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/2)） | — | 其他品牌（海信、创维等）应该也能用，但还没在真机上验证。欢迎[提交 Issue](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues) 或 PR 补充你的机型。 ## 已知限制 - **需要联网**：航拍按 1080p H.264 实时播放，码率约 15–20 Mbps；每日精选也要联网。 - **HDMI 设备名**：真实名称（如「Apple TV」）需要系统权限才读得到，所以只显示「已连接」。 - **TCL 音量条**：调音量时会同时弹出 TCL 自己的音量条，这是让音量真正生效的必要条件。 - **小米屏保**：停在别的 App 里空闲时，仍然会出现小米自己的屏保。 - **网页安装**：浏览器连不上电视的网络 ADB，电视的 USB 口也不能被电脑当成设备连接，所以没法「打开网页就装」。 ## 开发 需要 JDK 17、Android SDK 36。 ```bash ./gradlew assembleStandardRelease assembleGuardRelease BUILD=1 KEEP_ADB=1 TV=<电视IP> tools/install.sh # 用本地编译的 APK 安装 ``` - [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)：代码结构与数据流 - [docs/HANDOFF.md](docs/HANDOFF.md)：现状、调试技巧、必须遵守的规则 - [docs/devices/](docs/devices/)：各机型的实测笔记，包括 TCL 多屏互动的推送协议 - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)：给 AI 代理的开发说明 - [site/](site/)：官网（纯静态，中文 `/`、英文 `/en/`） 设计上的取舍：按 960×540dp 的画布等比缩放，不同密度的电视看起来一样；电视 GPU 很弱，每帧最多一次全屏绘制，空闲时不跑动画；焦点动画用弹簧，可以中途打断；字体用 Inter（OFL 许可）。 航拍目录 `app/src/main/assets/aerials.json` 由 Apple 公开的 `resources-16.tar` 生成，只有影片地址和地名，不含影片本身。 ## 许可 [MIT](LICENSE)。Inter 字体使用 [SIL Open Font License](FONT-LICENSE-OFL.txt)。 Aerial 是独立的开源项目，与 Apple、小米、TCL、索尼均无关联。航拍影片版权归 Apple 所有，由 Apple 的服务器直接播放；每日精选图片来自必应，版权归原作者所有。

items.description: GPU tensor unlock source for RTX 4090 and experimental RTX 4070 Ti SUPER; firmware generated locally
items.readme:
# GPU unlock 1.1.1 — RTX 4090, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER and RTX 4060 Ti 16GB

New to this project? Start with the [copy-paste Quick Start](QUICKSTART.md).

This Linux kernel module enables the SM speed-select override before the stock
NVIDIA driver starts. RTX 4090 (`10de:2684`, AD102) support has demonstrated
approximately **2× FP16 and BF16 tensor throughput with FP32 accumulation**:

| Mode | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP16 → FP32 accumulate | 165.6 TF/s | 331.6 TF/s |
| BF16 → FP32 accumulate | 165.5 TF/s | 330.6 TF/s |

The override survived PCIe Function Level Reset (FLR), stock NVIDIA `615.78.08`
initialization and CUDA benchmarks. INT8, `dp4a` and scalar FP32 stayed near their
baseline rates. The original transaction preceded the repository cleanup; see
the [technical report](rtx4090-register-report.md) and
[original evidence](docs/evidence/rtx4090/README.md).

An independent owner run of revision `8855e7b` also completed the RTX 4090
transaction and NVIDIA driver handoff on Linux `7.2.11-arch1-1`. Matched
stock/unlocked measurements with NVIDIA `615.78.08` and the same 450 W cap
found FP16/FP32 instruction throughput **160.4 → 320.4 TF/s** and BF16/FP32
**159.7 → 320.2 TF/s**. All exercised numerical checks passed. Real cuBLAS
GEMM median throughput varied by shape: FP16 gained 12–34%, BF16 gained
16–20% at two shapes and was essentially unchanged at 4096³. These are one
matched run pair with the desktop active, not whole-application speedups or
an extended stability test. See the [matched evidence and limits](docs/evidence/rtx4090-pr1-matched/README.md)
and [testing workflow](docs/testing.md).

A separate cold test of the Ada port on one RTX 4070 Ti SUPER
(`10de:2705`) with NVIDIA `580.178.04` measured FP16/FP32 tensor issue rate
at **95.0 → 189.9 TF/s** and BF16/FP32 at **95.0 → 189.7 TF/s** under the
same 240 W power cap. INT8 stayed at 379.5 TOP/s. The stock driver loaded,
the NVIDIA RM getter reported full FMLA32 rate, deterministic FP16/BF16 GEMM
outputs matched exactly, and owner mining recovered with fresh accepted shares.
A second matched instruction benchmark found **TF32/FP32 47.49 → 94.51 TF/s**
(1.99×), with its FP16/FP32 control also near 2×. Unsigned INT4/INT32 stayed
at approximately **754.8 TOP/s** in both states. These are register-resident
issue rates, not application GEMM or inference speedups.
A matched, verified E4M3 FP8/FP32 CUTLASS GEMM measured **59.326 TF/s stock →
59.495 TF/s unlocked** on this card, a 0.3% difference. This single GEMM did
not show a meaningful FP8 gain; other FP8 kernels remain untested.
This is one card; the unlock succeeded on two cold boots and two ordinary
warm reboots, the last from a persistent EFI default. Throughput was measured
on the first cold boot. See the [2705 canary report](docs/ada-2705-report.md)
and its [sanitized raw benchmark output](docs/evidence/ada2705/README.md).

The AD102 payload and its debug-booter analysis come from
**[TOTORONG/AD103_win_unlocker](https://huggingface.co/TOTORONG/AD103_win_unlocker)**.
This fork integrates that published payload into
**[Zagitta/gpu-unlock](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock)**'s Linux module,
firmware generation and boot packaging. The payload is essential to the result.

## Experimental Windows contribution — Latence.app

A separate [MSI RTX 4070 Ti AD104 Windows UEFI reference port](windows/ad104-msi/README.md)
records one successful manual boot with NVIDIA 616.56 and matched cuBLAS FP16/FP32
**+80.1%**, BF16/FP32 **+76.4%** measurements. It is tied to one captured MSI Z490
profile; it does **not** add AD104 admission to the Linux module. See the
[report and limitations](docs/ad104-windows-latence-app.md). No firmware/Windows/ROM
binaries or automatic boot installer are distributed. Contribution by **Latence.app**;
original upstream credits and licences are retained.

## Supported targets

The module selects the AD102 firmware and payload automatically for RTX 4090
`10de:2684`. The original GeForce/CMP GA102/GA104 device list and GA102 payload
are retained, along with the newer GA103/GA106 device list. Upstream reported
RTX 3090 success; this branch does not revalidate every legacy board.

RTX 4090 D (`10de:2685`) uses the AD102 path with the experimental opt-in
`gpu_unlock.rtx4090d_experimental=1`. Select cards with `gpu_unlock.targets=`.

The Ada port additionally recognizes RTX 4070 Ti SUPER
`10de:2705` as an **experimental AD103 target validated on one card**. It requires both
`gpu_unlock.ad103_experimental=1` and `gpu_unlock.targets=` set to that card's
single exact PCI address. `targets=all` never selects it. On the tested 2705,
two cold boots and later warm reboots confirmed driver 580.178.04 handoff and
full-rate readbacks; matched throughput was measured across stock and unlocked
boots. Other boards remain unverified.

RTX 4060 Ti 16GB `10de:2805` is an **experimental AD106 target validated on one
card**. It uses the same AD102-family payload and requires both
`gpu_unlock.ad106_experimental=1` and a single exact PCI address; `targets=all`
never selects it. On the tested card, one cold boot passed every marker,
permission, selector and post-FLR gate, the NVIDIA 595.99.02 driver loaded, and
the RM getter changed FMLA32, IMLA2 and IMLA4 from half to full rate. No
same-card stock throughput run has been made yet. See the
[2805 report](docs/ada-2805-report.md).
Other Ada IDs, professional RTX A-series and data-centre parts are not accepted.
Shared firmware across Ada chips does not establish support for untested cards.

The RTX 4090 path runs the signed firmware, checks the payload's completion marker and
required permissions, writes SS0 `0x88888888` and SS1 `0x8`, then performs FLR
before the unmodified NVIDIA driver binds. It requires the expected
effective speed-select readout before and after FLR. No patched NVIDIA driver or UEFI
application is needed. The payload uses instruction addresses derived from
published decrypted debug-booter analysis; the production booter is authenticated
and decrypted inside the GPU.

## Build and install

Clone the GPL-2.0-only source and build the packages locally so the pinned
NVIDIA firmware is downloaded and generated on your own machine:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/JustAResearcher/gpu-unlock-ada.git
cd gpu-unlock-ada
make install
```

`make install` detects the supported distribution family. Its explicit targets
are:

```sh
make install-arch   # makepkg -sif
make install-deb    # apt-get build-dep, dpkg-buildpackage, apt-get install
make install-rpm    # dnf builddep, rpmbuild, dnf install
```

`make arch`, `make deb` and `make rpm` build without installing. Packages are
built from the committed `HEAD`; Debian and RPM outputs go to `build/deb` and
`build/rpm`. Kernel headers and a working DKMS toolchain are required.

Builds fetch the pinned NVIDIA `610.43.03` source and binary inputs over HTTPS
and verify their SHA-256 hashes. `make inputs` prepares the cache;
`make firmware` generates assets from cached inputs; `make assets` does both.
The default cache is `$HOME/.cache/gpu-unlock` and can be overridden with
`CACHE=`, `INPUTS=` and `ASSETS=`. A clean-chroot Debian build needs
`GPU_UNLOCK_INPUTS` pointing to the input cache because `dpkg-buildpackage`
does not fetch inputs itself.

The source archive produced by `make dist`, the Debian source package and the
`.nosrc.rpm` contain no NVIDIA archives or generated firmware. See
[firmware/README.md](firmware/README.md) for the input and asset layout.
Prebuilt firmware packages are not distributed by this repository.

## Enable at boot

The package installs the module and firmware into the initramfs so the unlock
runs before NVIDIA binds the card. It remains inactive unless the kernel
command line opts in:

```text
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:03:00.0
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:03:00.0,0000:04:00.0
gpu_unlock.targets=all
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:01:00.0 gpu_unlock.ad103_experimental=1
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:01:00.0 gpu_unlock.ad106_experimental=1
```

These PCI addresses are examples. Use the full PCI names printed by `lspci -D`.
`all` selects every accepted unbound card, including legacy GA102/GA104 targets;
an explicit address is useful when selecting one RTX 4090. Do not mix `all` with
addresses. RTX 4070 Ti SUPER `10de:2705` and RTX 4060 Ti 16GB `10de:2805` each
require their own experimental flag and a single exact PCI address; `all` never
selects them. Invalid entries
are logged and ignored.

The packages support these initramfs generators:

- **mkinitcpio:** `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-gpu-unlock.conf` puts `gpu_unlock`
  immediately before `nvidia` in `MODULES`, or last if NVIDIA is absent. Images
  are rebuilt on installation. A custom configuration selected with `-c` or a
  preset `_config` does not read drop-ins; add `gpu_unlock` before `nvidia` in
  that configuration's `MODULES` yourself.
- **initramfs-tools:**
  `/usr/share/initramfs-tools/modules.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.
- **dracut:** `/usr/lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.

There is no `softdep nvidia pre:` rule because kmod uses only the first matching
soft dependency line, which can conflict with other packages.

**Power the machine off and start it again for the first attempt.** The module
needs a card whose firmware state is fresh before NVIDIA loads. A warm reboot
is not guaranteed to provide that state: it did on the tested
RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, where the pre-firmware WPR2 readback returned to zero and
the unlock succeeded again without an AC cut. Other boards may retain WPR2;
the module refuses to rerun the firmware sequence in that state. It also skips
cards that are already bound or powered down. If board firmware left bus
mastering enabled, the module clears it and verifies that it stayed cleared;
the later WPR2 check still rejects an already initialized card.
Loading the module manually after NVIDIA has bound the card cannot unlock it.

After validating a cold boot and a one-time warm reboot on the exact card, a
persistent bootloader entry can select the same early initramfs and exact
`gpu_unlock.*` options on every boot. A one-shot entry by itself does not
persist. Keep an unmodified stock entry available, and verify
`gpu_unlock: unlocked`, the rate readback and GPU health after each boot.
The tested canary uses a kernel-version-specific image; regenerate and
revalidate that image before removing its pinned kernel during an upgrade.

Avoid `nvidia-smi`, CUDA, NVML and `nvidia-modprobe` before a manual cold-card
attempt: they can load NVIDIA by name. Ordinary modprobe blacklist rules do not
block explicit named loads. The packaged initramfs flow avoids the need for
manual firmware staging and research parameters.

The original display-card handoff is retained: the firmware framebuffer is
removed just before FLR, and the display stays blank until `nvidia-drm` takes
over. Display handoff and multi-card operation were not part of the RTX 4090
validation.

## Check and disable

Inspect the kernel log after boot:

```sh
journalctl -k -b | grep gpu_unlock
lspci -nnk -s 0000:03:00.0  # replace the example address
```

A loaded module or successful `modprobe` return alone does not prove an unlock:
look for the selected card's `gpu_unlock: unlocked` message and the payload,
selector and post-FLR checks. The report describes independent register and
performance confirmation. The optional read-only sampler lives in
`diagnostics/peek`; the CUDA instruction benchmark is in `diagnostics/bench`.
Never load a second BAR0 sampler while `gpu_unlock` is performing its firmware
transaction.

If the module reports that firmware did not stop and its DMA buffers are being
kept, power off before trying again. The module intentionally retains buffers
that firmware may still use. Do not force-unload it in this state.

Remove `gpu_unlock.targets=` from the kernel command line to disable future
attempts. It can be removed for one boot in the bootloader editor. Removing the
packages removes the module and initramfs integration; power off to return to a
fresh hardware state.

## Development and credits

`make test` runs the host-side suite without accessing a GPU. Missing generated
firmware is reported as an explicit skip of the full transaction tests. After
`make assets`, use `make test-full` for a strict check that requires both the
pinned source and all generated assets. Override `ASSETS=` and `NVIDIA_SOURCE=`
for inputs built elsewhere. These tests mock firmware execution and device
behavior; they do not replace a hardware repeat.
See [testing and interpreting results](docs/testing.md) for the validation
levels, matched benchmark commands and recorded hardware evidence.

The kernel verifies each loaded asset against its pinned SHA-256 before claiming
the card or starting firmware DMA, including files staged into an initramfs.
The kernel's SHA-256 library (`CONFIG_CRYPTO_LIB_SHA256`) must be available.
`make -C kernel/gpu_unlock` builds against the running kernel's headers; use
`LLVM=1` when those headers support a Clang build.

The Linux module and packaging derive from
[Zagitta/gpu-unlock](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock). The AD102 four-PLM
payload derives from
[TOTORONG/AD103_win_unlocker](https://huggingface.co/TOTORONG/AD103_win_unlocker),
including its published payload generator and debug-booter analysis. The GA102
V67 chain derives from
[WildFlash1st/cmp90hx-unlock](https://github.com/WildFlash1st/cmp90hx-unlock).
The earlier CMP unlock work, NVIDIA's published loader code, Nouveau and
[envytools](https://github.com/envytools/envytools) also underpin the loader and
investigation.

The kernel module, packaging and payload integration are GPL-2.0-only. NVIDIA
firmware remains under its own terms. See [firmware/NOTICE.md](firmware/NOTICE.md)
and [licenses/](licenses/) for provenance and preserved license notices.

items.description: Capture iPhone LiDAR and photos, reconstruct editable Three.js rooms, and explore them in a browser.
items.readme:
# 3D Model Anything

[![Watch the video: 3D Model Anything](docs/images/thumb-1.png)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JGQCcCzuS88)

Capture a room on an iPhone, then use its geometry and photographs to build an editable Three.js scene with an AI coding agent.

[Open the office viewer](https://wesbos.github.io/3d-model-anything/) · [App support](https://wesbos.github.io/3d-model-anything/support.html)

This repository includes the **3D Model Anything iPhone app**, a **Three.js viewer**, the **scan-to-threejs agent skill**, and **Wes’s detailed office demo**.

The app records the evidence. The skill guides an agent through measurement, modeling and matched-camera visual comparisons. This is an iterative reconstruction workflow, not a one-click scan-to-perfect-model converter. The current workflow focuses on rooms and interiors.

## Run the viewer

Use Node.js 22.12+ (or a newer supported release).

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:5188. Explore the office in dollhouse, walking, overhead, wireframe and knolling views. The playground is at `/play.html?room=office-v4&mode=fpv`.

```sh
npm run build
npm run preview
```

The demo includes the reconstructed office and selected textures. Original scans and photo collections are not distributed; Scan and Overlay are disabled for this example. Those modes remain available for your own rooms with reference assets.

## Capture your own space

See [the iPhone app](apps/house-capture/README.md) for building with Xcode, device requirements, scanning and sharing. Scanning needs a LiDAR-equipped iPhone or iPad. Non-LiDAR devices can import and review scans.

The app is source-available here; an App Store release is a separate distribution step. Do not assume an App Store download is available yet.

Export a room or session through the system share sheet and extract it into an ignored `data/captures-in/<room>/` directory. Exports keep the existing `house-capture/5` contract; changing the app name does not change the files.

## Use the skill

The skill lives at `.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/SKILL.md`. Open this repository in an agent that supports local skills and ask it to use **scan-to-threejs** with your extracted export. You can also copy that skill directory into your agent's skill directory; the companion viewer/runtime in this repo is still needed for its capture workflow.

Example request:

> Use scan-to-threejs to rebuild the room in data/captures-in/my-room. Inspect the measurements and photos, create an editable scene, and compare rendered views with the original photographs.

Start with [the format guide](.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/references/house-capture.md) and [project layout](.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/references/project-layout.md). Helpers need Python 3; photo comparisons need Pillow, and optional depth reconstruction needs NumPy, Open3D and Pillow. Capture scripts use the `agent-browser` CLI.

A new room goes in `demos/<id>/` and is registered in `demos/index.ts`. The office example retains its earlier reconstruction layers (`office-v2`, `office-latest`, `office-v4`) to preserve the final geometry.

## Privacy and licensing

Only the office example is distributed. No other rooms, connected-house layout, original scan bundles, or development Git history are included. Keep your captures private; inspect assets before publishing your own demo.

Reusable source code and the skill are MIT licensed. The supplied office images/textures have separate [asset terms](ASSETS-LICENSE.md). Third-party marks, artwork and depicted products are not licensed by the code license.

See [release status](docs/release-status.md) for validation and iPhone distribution steps.

items.name: hatchzip
items.description: HatchZip is a free, open-source archive extractor for Windows, macOS and Linux that extracts ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar and split archives in place, so it needs free space for the extracted files only. Desktop app and CLI.
items.readme:
HatchZip

Extract huge archives in place. The archive shrinks as your files hatch,
so you only need free space for the output, not for the output and the archive.

Installation | Usage | Safety | How it works | Contributing

A 180 GB game download that unpacks to 200 GB needs 380 GB of disk with WinRAR, 7-Zip or `unzip`, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB. It extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive file as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files. It checks that the extraction will fit before it changes anything, keeps a safety margin of free space the whole way through, and can be stopped or crash at any moment and pick up where it left off. It reads ZIP, 7z, tar, `.tar.gz`, RAR volume sets and split archives. ### Get it > [!IMPORTANT] > HatchZip is only distributed from this repository's [releases](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases) and its site, [hatchzip.dev](https://hatchzip.dev). Other sites using the name, such as hatchzip.com, are not affiliated with this project. No coding needed. **[Download for Windows](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe)** (Windows 10 and 11), or for [macOS (Apple Silicon)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg), [macOS (Intel)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg) and [Linux](#installation). 1. Run the installer. Windows may show "Windows protected your PC" because HatchZip is not code-signed yet: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. 2. Right-click the archive, choose **HatchZip**, then **Extract here**. On Windows 11 the menu is under **Show more options**. 3. Or open HatchZip from the Start menu, open the archive, and choose **Extract**. HatchZip shows whether the files will fit before it changes anything. The archive is used up as the files come out, so when it finishes, only the extracted files are left. To keep the archive when there is room for both, choose **Extract here (keep archive)** in the right-click menu, or clear **Remove the archive during extraction** in the app. That is a normal extraction: the archive is not changed, and space is required for all extracted files. ## Highlights The same 200 MB of game data (21 files), packed by the real tools, extracted on a 220 MiB disk with about 50 MB free: | Archive | `unzip` / 7-Zip | HatchZip | |---|---|---| | ZIP, 180 MB | `unzip` ran out of space at file 6 of 21 | Finished, every file byte-identical | | 7z from 7-Zip 25.01, `-ms=20m` (10 solid blocks) | Needs 380 MB | Finished in 0.64 s, every file byte-identical | | 7z split into 5 volumes of 40 MB | Needs 380 MB | Finished; volumes deleted one at a time, peak 210 MB used | | tar from GNU tar, 200 MB | Needs 400 MB | Finished in 0.12 s, every file byte-identical | | 7z from 7-Zip with default settings (1 solid block) | Needs 380 MB | Refused before touching anything: one solid block can't be freed until all of it is out, so it needs 200 MB free | | | Result | |---|---| | ZIP extraction speed, same data | 0.25 to 0.35 s, against 1.48 to 1.50 s for `unzip` 6.00, including an fsync `unzip` skips | | Crash safety | Killed at both unsafe moments of a batch at many points of each format's run; every resume finished with identical output | | Works on | Any filesystem that can shrink a file: ext4, btrfs, XFS, NTFS, APFS, and also exFAT and FAT32 USB drives | Measured on Fedora 43, Intel Core i7-14700HX, SK Hynix NVMe SSD, warm page cache; the disk-space runs used a 220 MiB tmpfs to stand in for a full laptop disk, the speed runs ext4. Speed comes from decompressing files in parallel, so an archive holding one giant file extracts at the speed of a single core. The extra space HatchZip needs beyond the output is about the size of the largest single unit it can free at once: one file for ZIP and tar, one solid block for 7z. On filesystems that can punch holes (ext4, XFS, btrfs, tmpfs; NTFS and APFS not yet verified), a large file stored or deflated in a ZIP, or in a tar, frees its archive bytes every 256 MiB while it is extracted: a ZIP holding one 600 MiB stored file extracted on a 950 MiB tmpfs with 367 MB free, where it needed 629 MB before. `hatchzip check` computes the exact figure for any archive. ## Installation ### Desktop app Download from the [latest release](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest): | System | File | |---|---| | Windows 10 and 11 (x64) | [`HatchZip-x64-setup.exe`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe): installs per user, no admin rights, adds the right-click menu | | macOS, Apple Silicon | [`HatchZip-aarch64.dmg`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg) | | macOS, Intel | [`HatchZip-x86_64.dmg`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg) | | Debian, Ubuntu | [`hatchzip_amd64.deb`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/hatchzip_amd64.deb) | | Fedora, openSUSE | [`hatchzip-x86_64.rpm`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/hatchzip-x86_64.rpm) | | Any Linux | [`HatchZip-x86_64.AppImage`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.AppImage) | The installers also put the `hatchzip` command (and its short name `hz`) on your `PATH`. The Windows setup and the macOS apps are not code-signed yet: on Windows choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**; on macOS 15 and later, open the app once, then allow it under System Settings, Privacy & Security. ### Command line only Linux and macOS: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.sh | sh ``` Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` Both download the build for your machine from the latest release, check it against its published SHA-256 checksum, and install `hatchzip` and `hz` for your user only, with the man page and shell completions. No root or administrator rights. Every release file from 0.1.3 on carries signed build provenance. To check that a download really was built from this repository by its release workflow, wherever you got it: ```sh gh attestation verify HatchZip-x64-setup.exe --repo xevrion/hatchzip ``` ### Package managers Homebrew and Scoop are live. winget is in review, and the AUR packages are coming soon; until they are listed as live here, a package under those names does not come from this project. | System | Command | Installs | |---|---|---| | Arch Linux (AUR) | `yay -S hatchzip-bin`, or `yay -S hatchzip` to build from source | App and CLI | | Windows (winget) | `winget install Xevrion.HatchZip` | App and CLI, same as the setup | | Windows (Scoop) | `scoop bucket add xevrion https://github.com/xevrion/scoop-bucket`, then `scoop install xevrion/hatchzip` | CLI | | macOS and Linux (Homebrew) | `brew install xevrion/tap/hatchzip` | CLI | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install --cask xevrion/tap/hatchzip` | App and CLI | ### With Cargo ```sh cargo install hatchzip ``` This builds the command line tool from [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/hatchzip). The engine is a library too: [`hatchzip-core`](https://crates.io/crates/hatchzip-core). It reads every format but RAR; `cargo install hatchzip --features rar` adds RAR support, which compiles UnRAR's C++ source under its own [license](#license) and needs a C++ compiler. ### From source With [Rust](https://rustup.rs) (the version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and installed automatically): ```sh git clone https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip.git cd hatchzip cargo build --release ``` The binaries are `target/release/hatchzip` and `target/release/hatchzip-gui` (`.exe` on Windows). Building the desktop app on Linux needs the fontconfig headers (`libfontconfig1-dev` or `fontconfig-devel`). `cargo build --release --features rar` adds RAR support, as in the release builds; it needs a C++ compiler. ### Shell completions and man page ```sh hatchzip completions bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/hatchzip hatchzip completions zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_hatchzip" hatchzip completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/hatchzip.fish hatchzip completions powershell >> $PROFILE hatchzip man > ~/.local/share/man/man1/hatchzip.1 # then: man hatchzip ``` ## Usage ### See whether it fits ```sh hatchzip check game.zip ``` ``` game.zip 180.2 MB zip, 200.0 MB uncompressed in 22 entries available 50.5 MB standard extraction needs 200.0 MB required 29.9 MB (+5.0 MB reserved) available after 30.6 MB ``` `check` reads the archive's index and the disk's free space and changes nothing. "Standard extraction needs" is what extracting while keeping the archive requires; when that fits too, `check` says so. `hatchzip check game.zip --keep-archive` shows the plan for keeping it. ### Extract ```sh hatchzip extract game.zip # into ./game/ hatchzip extract game.zip -o D:\Games\Foo # somewhere else hatchzip x game.7z.001 # split archive; any part's name works ``` HatchZip prints the same space plan, asks for confirmation, then extracts. When the extraction is complete, the archive has been removed and the files are in the output folder. For a split archive, each volume is deleted as soon as everything in it is extracted. | Option | Effect | |---|---| | `-o, --output ` | Output folder. Defaults to a folder named after the archive, next to it. It may hold other files, but none where the archive's files go. | | `--keep-archive` | Keep the archive: a normal extraction that removes nothing. Space is required for all extracted files. No confirmation is asked. | | `--keep-free ` | Free space HatchZip never uses, such as `500MB` or `10GB`. Default `2GB`, so the disk never fills to zero. | | `--verify-first` | Read the whole archive and check every file's checksum before deleting anything. Takes extra time, recommended for downloads you can't easily get again. | | `-y, --yes` | Skip the confirmation prompt. Required when not run from a terminal, unless `--keep-archive` is given. | | `-q, --quiet` | Print only errors and prompts. | ### Keep the archive ```sh hatchzip extract game.zip --keep-archive ``` When the disk has room for the archive and all its files, `--keep-archive` extracts like any other tool and leaves the archive byte for byte as it was, for when it is needed again. The space check, path and collision checks, checksums and password handling are the same as for an extraction in place. If keeping the archive does not fit, HatchZip says so, by how much, and what extracting in place would require instead. An interrupted run resumes like any other, and goes on keeping the archive even when resumed without `--keep-archive`. An extraction that started in place cannot switch to keeping the archive, since part of it is already removed. `hatchzip restore` on an archive being kept only discards the progress: the archive was never changed. ### Several archives ```sh hatchzip extract a.zip b.7z c.tar.gz ``` The archives are extracted one after another, each into its own folder, or all into the folder given with `-o`. The space for each one is checked just before it starts, so the space one archive frees is available to the next. The first archive that does not complete stops the run, and HatchZip lists which archives were extracted, which one stopped and whether its progress is saved, and which were not started; the exit status is that archive's. `check`, `test` and `list` also take several archives, go through all of them, and exit with the status of the first one that did not succeed. Naming every volume of a split archive, as a shell pattern like `game.7z.*` does, counts as that archive once. ### Stop and resume Press `Ctrl+C` and HatchZip finishes the files it is writing, saves its progress and exits. A second `Ctrl+C` quits immediately, which is also safe. To continue, run the same command again: ```sh hatchzip extract game.zip ``` The same applies after a crash, a power cut, or running out of space because something else filled the disk. Progress lives in two small files next to the archive, `game.zip.hatchzip` and `game.zip.hatchzip-tail`. **Do not delete them while an extraction is unfinished**: they hold the archive's index, which is no longer inside the archive itself. ### Stop for good To give up on an unfinished extraction instead, restore the archive: ```sh hatchzip restore game.zip ``` What is left of the archive becomes a normal archive again, holding exactly the entries not yet extracted, which 7-Zip, WinRAR, `unzip` or `tar` open as usual. The files already extracted stay in the output folder. Restore only appends a new index, so it needs only the free space that index takes, and if it is interrupted, running it again finishes it. ### List and test ```sh hatchzip list game.7z # what's inside, with sizes hatchzip test game.7z # read every file and verify its checksum, writing nothing ``` Plain tar has no checksums for file contents, so `test` on a tar only proves every file can be read in full. ### Exit status | Code | Meaning | |---|---| | 0 | Success | | 1 | Failure. If extraction had started, progress is saved. | | 2 | Invalid command line | | 3 | Not enough free space. Nothing was changed. | | 4 | The archive is damaged. Nothing was deleted. | | 5 | The archive is password protected and no correct password was given. | | 130 | Paused with Ctrl+C. Run the same command to continue. | With several archives, the status is that of the first archive that did not succeed. ## Is it safe HatchZip destroys the archive as it extracts, so it is built around never losing a file that has not safely landed on disk. - **Nothing changes until the plan fits.** The space check runs before the first byte is touched, and it replays the whole extraction to find the moment that needs the most free space, not just the total. - **A file is written, flushed to the physical disk and renamed into place before the part of the archive holding it is cut off.** A crash at any point leaves either the file or its bytes in the archive, never neither. - **Damage stops the run where it is.** Every file's CRC-32 is checked as it is extracted. A damaged file is not written, and it stays in the archive along with everything before it. - **Hostile archives are refused before anything is deleted:** paths that escape the output folder, entries that overlap each other, entries that appear twice, and links where other entries need a folder. Setuid and setgid bits are never restored, and symlinks are created only after every regular file is written, so nothing can be written through one. - **A kept archive stays as it was.** With `--keep-archive`, the code that shrinks, frees or deletes archive bytes refuses to run for the whole extraction, and its progress file has a format older versions refuse, so none of them can resume it in place. What it cannot protect against: if the download itself is damaged, the files before the damaged spot are extracted and the archive is partly gone. Use `--verify-first` when the archive can't be downloaded again. On btrfs or APFS, space held by a snapshot that includes the archive is not freed until the snapshot is deleted. ## Supported formats | Format | Status | Freed in steps of | |---|---|---| | ZIP, ZIP64, self-extracting `.exe` ZIPs | Supported. Tested: Stored, Deflate, Deflate64, bzip2, LZMA, PPMd, XZ and Zstandard, including archives made by 7-Zip itself, and entries past the 4 GiB mark. | One file | | 7z, solid and non-solid | Supported. Tested with archives made by 7-Zip 25.01: LZMA2 (its default), LZMA, BCJ with LZMA2, bzip2, Deflate and PPMd; Zstandard with an archive made by py7zr, since 7-Zip has no Zstandard coder for the 7z format. | One solid block | | tar (uncompressed) | Supported, including long names, symlinks and hard links | One file | | `.tar.gz`, `.tgz` | Supported, including multi-member gzip (`bgzip`, `pigz -i`) and split `.tar.gz.001` sets. Extracted from the front, freeing the compressed bytes behind the decoder where the filesystem can punch holes; every gzip CRC-32 and length is checked before anything is touched. Tested with archives from GNU tar with gzip, and pigz. Elsewhere (FAT32, exFAT) it still extracts and resumes, but needs room for the archive and every file at once, and `check` says so. | 256 MiB of output | | Split archives (`.001`, `.002`, ...) of ZIP or 7z, as 7-Zip makes them | Supported | One file or block; each volume is deleted once emptied | | Password-protected ZIP (ZipCrypto and AES) and 7z (AES, including encrypted file lists) | Supported. HatchZip asks for the password, or takes `--password` or `HATCHZIP_PASSWORD`, and proves it on one file before anything is deleted. It is never saved, so a resumed run asks again. | Same as unencrypted | | `.tar.zst`, `.tar.xz` | Refused before extraction, planned; see [the format notes](docs/formats.md#tarzst-and-tarxz). | | | One huge solid 7z block | Works, but needs free space for the whole block, as the table above shows. Freeing space inside a block is the same planned technique. | | | RAR, RAR 5 and RAR 4, single files and volume sets (`.part1.rar`, `.part2.rar`, ... or `.rar`, `.r00`, ...) | Supported in the release builds, decoded by UnRAR (see [License](#license)); builds without the `rar` feature, such as `cargo install hatchzip`, refuse RAR before anything is touched. Password-protected files work as for ZIP: a RAR 5 password is proven by its check value, a RAR 4 one by decoding the smallest encrypted file, which for a large file can take a while. A large stored file is freed while it is written, as in tar. Refused before anything is touched: encrypted file names, links, dictionaries over 4 GB, and sets with a volume missing or a stray one after the last. `restore` works. Tested with archives made by RAR 6.24 (RAR 5 and RAR 4) and archives written by the test suite; sets made by WinRAR 7.23 were tested on Windows when RAR support was first written. | One file; a volume once every file that reaches into it is out | | Solid RAR | Extracted only while the archive is kept (`--keep-archive`): a solid archive decodes front to back in one pass and UnRAR can't save its state, so it can't be freed as it goes or resumed mid-way. In place, it is refused before anything is touched. | | | Native split ZIP (`.z01`) | Planned | | ## How it works ZIP, 7z and tar all store their contents as a sequence of independent pieces: files for ZIP and tar, solid blocks for 7z. ZIP and 7z keep their index at the very end. HatchZip saves that index to a side file, then extracts pieces starting from the last one in the archive. After each batch it truncates the archive to where that batch began, which every operating system and filesystem supports; for a split archive, that means deleting whole volumes and shortening one. RAR stores files one after another like tar, so it is freed file by file too, and a volume is deleted once every file reaching into it is out. A `.tar.gz` is one compressed stream that can only be decoded from the front, so HatchZip extracts it front to back and punches holes in the compressed bytes it has used, at resume points it can restart from after a crash. The full design, including the exact order of writes that makes a crash safe, is in [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md). ## How it is built HatchZip is written with the help of AI coding assistants, and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is the rulebook they work under. It is the strict part of the project: the tool deletes its own input, so a change only lands with proof. - **More than 130 tests run on Linux, macOS and Windows** for every change, in CI on real machines of each kind. - **Crash tests kill the process at every step** where it writes a file, saves its progress or cuts the archive, then resume and compare every extracted file byte for byte. - **Freeing space is checked, not assumed.** CI fails if ext4, APFS or NTFS do not really give the space back. - **Damaged and hostile archives are part of the suite:** paths that escape the folder, overlapping entries, bad CRCs, truncated downloads, wrong passwords. - **Every number in this README was measured** on real hardware, and the conditions are written next to it. Pull requests and bug reports from people are held to the same rules, and are very welcome. ## Star history ## License HatchZip is licensed under either of [Apache License, Version 2.0](LICENSE-APACHE) or [MIT license](LICENSE-MIT), at your option. RAR archives are decoded by the UnRAR source code, which is freeware under its own [license](LICENSE-UNRAR): free to use for extracting RAR archives, but not to build a RAR compatible archiver. It is compiled in only with the `rar` cargo feature, which is off by default, so `cargo install hatchzip`, the crates on crates.io and distribution builds are open source throughout and need no C++ compiler. The release builds on the [releases page](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases) have it on, and every release download includes `LICENSE-UNRAR`. ## Contributing Bug reports, especially from filesystems and operating systems not covered by CI, are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in HatchZip by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

11 Claude skills for day trading: scan thousands of charts, track breaking news, time every entry and exit, and replay every outcome before you risk a dollar.

Free, MIT, no signup, no API key. The tools are plain Python that read free
public data: Yahoo Finance charts, Nasdaq Trader's symbol lists, SEC EDGAR
and the House Clerk.

One scans thousands of charts for setups. Another tracks breaking news on
every stock you watch. One watches a setup bar by bar and tells you the moment
to get in, and another sets your stop and your target before you do. And the
craziest one is the Time Machine: before you risk a dollar, it replays the
rest of the session 10,000 times from the stock's own recent bars, plus every
past day the same setup fired, and tells you the honest odds.

And no trade goes through until you say yes. Nothing in this pack can place
an order on its own. Paper trading is the default.

> **Looking for the original Trader skill?** Copy an investor's 13F, the
> stock screener, tax lots and rebalancing live in
> [github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill).
> This repo is its day-trading sequel: the Trader skill v2.

## Install

Paste this into Claude:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill
/plugin install day-trader-skill@day-trader-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/day-trader-skill:trader-scanner` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/trader-scanner`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill.git
cp -r day-trader-skill/trader-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the
top of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the Python tools, but the method
works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install. The SEC tools
(news filings, the analyst) ask you to identify yourself: put your name and
email in `trader/config.json` (`"sec_user_agent": "Your Name you@example.com"`)
or in the `SEC_USER_AGENT` environment variable.

## The eleven

| command | job | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/trader-scanner` | Chart Scanner | Scans thousands of charts for setups: opening-range breakouts, flags, oversold bounces. |
| `/trader-news` | News Monitor | Tracks breaking news on every stock you watch and flags what moves it. |
| `/trader-entry` | Entry Timer | Watches a setup bar by bar and tells you the moment to get in. |
| `/trader-exit` | Exit Planner | Sets your stop and your target before you enter, so you know when to get out. |
| `/trader-timemachine` | Time Machine | Replays every possible outcome of a trade before you risk a dollar: 10,000 simulated sessions plus every past time the setup fired. |
| `/trader-risk` | Risk Manager | Checks every trade against your limits and stops anything over them. |
| `/trader-budget` | Budget Manager | Sizes every position to your budget and your max loss per trade. |
| `/trader-broker` | Order Executor | Sends approved orders to your broker, paper trading by default, never without your yes. |
| `/trader-alerts` | Price Alerts | Rings when a price, a stop or the opening bell hits. |
| `/trader-analyst` | Earnings Analyst | Reads earnings reports and sums up what changed. |
| `/trader-pelosi` | Pelosi Tracker | Reads Congress's stock-trade disclosures the minute they are filed. |

## How to use it

Everything lands in a `trader/` folder in your project, and each skill reads
what the last one wrote:

```
scanner -> news -> entry -> exit -> timemachine -> budget -> risk -> broker   (one trade)
alerts: stop, target, flat by the close                                       (while it is open)
news / analyst / pelosi                                                        (on a schedule)
```

An example, the trade in the reel: Tesla, Monday October 19 2026, real data.

1. **`/trader-scanner`** at 10:15 AM ET: of the 231 charts in the reel's
   scan, 42 had closed above their 15-minute opening range. TSLA is one: range 354.47 to 362.18,
   the 10:10 candle closed at 364.18, 0.55 % over the top.
2. **`/trader-news`**: the morning's TSLA headlines, in New York time
   ("Tesla-SpaceX Merger Mania Strikes Wall Street Ahead of Earnings", 8:04,
   tagged earnings and deal). Tesla reports this week: a day trade is out
   before the close, so it is not exposed to the report.
3. **`/trader-entry`** watched TSLA bar by bar. At 10:12 it said waiting (the
   10:10 bar was still forming). At 10:15 it said triggered: the first
   5-minute close above the range, 364.18.
4. **`/trader-exit`** set the plan before the entry: stop at the range's
   midpoint, 358.32, so 5.86 a share at risk; target one times that risk,
   370.04; flat by 3:55 PM either way.
5. **`/trader-timemachine`** replayed the rest of the day 10,000 times, each
   5-minute candle drawn from TSLA's own candles at that time of day over the
   previous 59 sessions (seed 19, so anyone can repeat it): target first
   29.4 %, stop first 25.5 %, still open at the close 45.1 %. It also re-ran
   the same rule on those 59 real sessions: it fired 33 times, 13 hit the
   target, 15 the stop, 5 neither. Its verdict: close to a coin flip. That is
   the point of looking before you risk a dollar.
6. **`/trader-budget`** with a $5,000 account and a $50 max loss per trade:
   50 / 5.86 = 8 shares ($2,913.44). If the stop fills at 358.32, the loss is
   $46.88. It writes one bracket order: buy 8 TSLA, stop-loss 358.32,
   take-profit 370.04.
7. **`/trader-risk`** checks it against your limits: the max loss, the daily
   loss limit, trades per day, reward to risk, the entry window, position
   size and cash. PASS or BLOCK, with the reason.
8. **`/trader-broker`** shows you the ticket in plain words. You type yes for
   that exact order. Claude calls your brokerage connector (Alpaca's MCP
   server, paper account by default), and Claude's own "Allow once / Deny"
   card asks you one more time.
9. **`/trader-alerts`** rings on the stop, the target and at 3:55 PM to
   flatten whatever is still open.

## The tools

All standard-library Python. The data tools read public endpoints and are
polite about it.

```bash
python3 trader-scanner/scan.py universe                                # ~5,900 US stocks, Nasdaq Trader
python3 trader-scanner/scan.py daily                                   # pre-market setups, whole universe
python3 trader-scanner/scan.py orb --at 10:15                          # opening-range breakouts so far
python3 trader-news/news.py --tickers TSLA --hours 12                  # headlines, 8-Ks, today's move
python3 trader-entry/entry.py check TSLA --setup orb                   # waiting / triggered / expired
python3 trader-entry/entry.py watch TSLA --every 30                    # bar by bar until it triggers
python3 trader-exit/exit.py plan --stop or-mid --target 1R --write     # -> trader/plan.json
python3 trader-timemachine/timemachine.py run --write                  # 10,000 replays + the history
python3 trader-budget/size.py --write                                  # -> trader/orders.json
python3 trader-risk/check.py                                           # PASS / BLOCK per order
python3 trader-broker/ticket.py show                                   # the tickets, READY or not
python3 trader-alerts/alerts.py add --from-plan                        # stop, target, flat by close
python3 trader-alerts/alerts.py check                                  # rings what hit, once
python3 trader-analyst/facts.py TSLA                                   # quarters, growth, EPS
python3 trader-pelosi/ptr.py index --member pelosi                     # her PTRs this year
```

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The tests run offline, on fixtures cut from real data: TSLA's 5-minute bars
for the 60 days to October 19 2026, the 10:15 AM opening-range scan, Yahoo's
TSLA headlines that morning, the House Clerk's 2026 index, real PTR text and
real XBRL facts. They reproduce every number in the example above.

## Fine print

**Not financial advice.** This is software that reads public data and does
arithmetic. It does not know your situation and it cannot see the future.
Most people who day trade lose money. You can lose money. Decide for
yourself, and talk to a licensed professional if you need advice.

**No trade goes through until you say yes.** Only `/trader-broker` can lead to
an order, and only after `/trader-risk` passes that exact order and you type
yes for it in the chat. Set your brokerage tool to "Needs approval" in Claude
(Customize, Connectors, tool permissions), never "Always allow", so Claude's
own "Allow once / Deny" card is a second check. No options, margin, short
selling or leverage unless you turn them on.

**Paper first.** `"paper": true` is the default in `config.example.json`, and
Alpaca's MCP server defaults to its paper account. Keys live in environment
variables, never in the chat.

**The Time Machine is a simulation, not a prediction.** It is built from the
stock's own last 60 days of 5-minute bars. The future can do things those 60
days never did: an earnings report, a halt, a headline. Treat its odds as a
reality check, never as a promise.

**A stop is a plan, not a guarantee.** In a fast market or across a gap, a
stop order can fill well past its price. The max loss shown is the loss at
the stop price.

**The data is free and unofficial.** Yahoo Finance's chart endpoint is not an
official API: it can lag, change or rate-limit you. The scanner and the entry
timer read 1-minute or 5-minute bars, not every tick. Check anything that
matters against your broker before you act on it.

**Day-trading rules.** FINRA removed the $25,000 pattern-day-trader minimum
on June 4, 2026 (Regulatory Notice 26-10), and brokers may phase the change
in until October 20, 2027, so yours may still apply the old rule. If it does,
set `"pdt_guard": true` and `/trader-risk` counts your day trades.

**Congress's trades are public, not inside information.** Members must disclose
trades over $1,000 within 45 days (the STOCK Act). The Pelosi skill reads those
public filings the minute they post.

**Taxes.** Day-trading gains are short-term gains, and frequent trading makes
wash sales likely. Nothing here is tax advice.

## Files

```
trader-scanner/     SKILL.md, scan.py
trader-news/        SKILL.md, news.py
trader-entry/       SKILL.md, entry.py
trader-exit/        SKILL.md, exit.py
trader-timemachine/ SKILL.md, timemachine.py
trader-risk/        SKILL.md, check.py
trader-budget/      SKILL.md, size.py, config.example.json, targets.example.json
trader-broker/      SKILL.md, ticket.py, claude_desktop_config.example.json
trader-alerts/      SKILL.md, alerts.py, alerts.example.json
trader-analyst/     SKILL.md, facts.py, metrics.example.json
trader-pelosi/      SKILL.md, ptr.py
tests/              unittest suite + offline fixtures
```

items.readme:
php2shell

CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619 — Independent Research & Verification

--- Two critical pre-authentication RCE vulnerabilities in PHP core, exploiting `session.upload_progress` (enabled by default) and the memory allocator's OOM bailout. **14 years of vulnerable code** (PHP 5.4.0, 2012 — present). **Author:** [Qi Deng](https://github.com/ikow)  |  **Writeup:** [qideng.substack.com](https://qideng.substack.com/p/php2shell-dissecting-phps-critical)  |  **Date:** 2026-10-21 ## Impact | What | Scale | |------|-------| | Websites running PHP | **78%** of all websites | | WordPress alone | **43%** of all websites | | Affected versions | PHP 5.4.0 through 8.5.11 (14 years) | | Authentication required | **None** | | Application vulnerability required | **None** (Chain D — mod_php) | ## Verified Attack Chains ### Chain A — Session File Injection + LFI → RCE Upload a file with PHP code in the filename → `session.upload_progress` stores it raw in the session file → include via any LFI → code execution. ``` Conditions: upload_progress=On (default) + application has LFI Reliability: 100% ``` ### Chain B — var_destroy UAF → Handler Overwrite → RCE `var_destroy()` frees back-reference chunks then fires `__destruct` without `serialize_lock`. Inner `unserialize()` reuses the freed var_hash → heap-use-after-free → overwrite function handler → RCE. ``` Conditions: application calls unserialize() with controlled data ASAN: heap-use-after-free CONFIRMED at var_unserializer.c:851 ``` ### Chain C — Session Handler Mismatch → `__destruct` → RCE Session written with `php_serialize` handler (pipe `|` preserved in filename) → read by `php` handler → splits at `|` → deserializes injected object → `__destruct` fires during var_hash cleanup **even when decode returns FAILURE**. ``` Conditions: two directories with different session.serialize_handler Key finding: __destruct fires on BOTH success and failure paths ``` ### Chain D — mod_php OOM → Stale EG() → RCE ⚡ Multipart POST triggers OOM during request startup → `longjmp()` skips `init_executor` → Apache mod_php runs shutdown on stale `EG()` globals → use-after-free → RCE. ``` Conditions: NONE — any PHP endpoint on Apache mod_php SAPI: Apache mod_php ✅ | FPM ⚠️ (child exits) | FrankenPHP ✅ ``` **This is a pre-auth, zero-dependency RCE against default Apache mod_php installations.** ### Chain E — FPM Session OOM → Stale BG(unserialize) → RCE ⚡ Producer request: `session_start()` decodes ~30MB session → OOM during `php_var_unserialize` → `BG(unserialize).level` stays >0, session destruction state dirty → FPM worker **survives**. Consumer request: `upload_progress` triggers `rfc1867` handler (runs **before** `PHP_RINIT_FUNCTION(basic)`) → accesses stale `BG(unserialize)` → "Session object destruction failed" → `__destruct` on stale objects → UAF → RCE. ``` Conditions: session_start() endpoint + large session file + FPM Key finding: rfc1867 runs BEFORE basic_rinit — stale BG(unserialize) is accessible Verified: "Session object destruction failed" during PHP Request Startup ``` ## Official CVE Details | CVE | GHSA | Description | |-----|------|-------------| | CVE-2026-109618 | [GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) | RCE via OOM corruption — `longjmp()` leaves request state invalid | | CVE-2026-109619 | [GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) | RCE via stale global state — worker retains freed request memory | **Patch:** [Commit 3584a98](https://github.com/php/php-src/commit/3584a98bda) — 300 files changed, replaces `longjmp()` with delayed soft OOM + hard `_exit()`. ## Quick Start ```bash # Clone git clone https://github.com/ikow/php2shell-poc.git && cd php2shell-poc # Start lab (PHP-FPM + nginx + Apache mod_php) cd lab && docker compose up -d # Verify Chain A: Session injection python3 ../poc/verify_session_injection.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080 # Verify Chain B: UAF (requires ASAN build) USE_ZEND_ALLOC=0 ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0" php ../poc/verify_uaf_asan.php # Verify Chain C: Handler mismatch python3 ../poc/verify_handler_mismatch.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080 # Verify Chain D: OOM on Apache mod_php python3 ../poc/verify_oom_trigger.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18081 --strategy headers # Verify Chain E: FPM stale BG state python3 ../poc/verify_fpm_stale_state.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080 ``` ## Repository Structure ``` php2shell-poc/ ├── README.md ├── poc/ │ ├── verify_session_injection.py # Chain A: session file injection │ ├── verify_uaf_asan.php # Chain B: var_destroy UAF (ASAN) │ ├── verify_handler_mismatch.py # Chain C: handler mismatch │ ├── verify_oom_trigger.py # Chain D: OOM trigger strategies │ └── verify_fpm_stale_state.py # Chain E: FPM stale BG verification ├── lab/ │ ├── docker-compose.yml # FPM + nginx + Apache mod_php │ ├── setup.sh # One-click lab setup │ ├── php.ini # FPM configuration │ └── php-apache.ini # Apache mod_php (low memory for OOM) └── docs/ ├── ANALYSIS.md # Full technical analysis └── cover.png # Cover image ``` ## Mitigation ```ini ; Immediate — reduces attack surface but does NOT fix all chains session.upload_progress.enabled = Off session.use_only_cookies = On ``` | Mitigation | Chains blocked | |-----------|---------------| | `session.upload_progress.enabled = Off` | A, C, E (partial) | | `session.use_only_cookies = On` | A, C (session fixation) | | `memory_limit` + `post_max_size` tuning | D (reduces OOM surface) | | Update to PHP 8.2.35+ | **All chains** | > **The only complete fix is patching PHP.** The OOM corruption (Chain D) is in the Zend engine core, not in session handling. ## Timeline | Date | Event | |------|-------| | 2012-03-01 | `session.upload_progress` introduced in PHP 5.4.0 | | 2026-10-20 | Details leaked before embargo; PHP advances release | | 2026-10-21 | PHP 8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12 released | | 2026-10-21 | This research published | ## References - [PHP Security Advisory](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php) - [GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) — CVE-2026-109618 - [GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) — CVE-2026-109619 - [Patch commit](https://github.com/php/php-src/commit/3584a98bda) — 300 files, Zend engine + extensions - [PR #22113](https://github.com/php/php-src/pull/22113) — Session fixation fix - [BleepingComputer coverage](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/php-ships-emergency-patches-for-critical-php2shell-flaws/) ## Disclaimer This repository contains **verification POCs only** — tools to confirm whether a system is vulnerable. No weaponized exploits are included. Full exploit code is available to [paid subscribers](https://qideng.substack.com/p/php2shell-dissecting-phps-critical). For authorized security testing and educational purposes only. ## License MIT

# 手机去广告 关掉国产安卓手机系统里的广告、热搜、资讯推荐和营销推送。 介绍页：**https://rddmwmddr.github.io/android-ad-cleaner/** ## 下载桌面客户端 插上手机，点几下按钮。不需要 Python，也不需要 AI 工具。 | 电脑 | 下载 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | Mac · Apple 芯片（M1 及以后） | [AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.0-mac-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases/download/v0.2.0/AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.0-mac-arm64.dmg) | 已签名、通过苹果公证，双击就能打开 | | Mac · Intel 芯片 | [AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.0-mac-intel.dmg](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases/download/v0.2.0/AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.0-mac-intel.dmg) | 同上 | | Windows 10 / 11 · 安装版 | [AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.0-windows-setup.exe](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases/download/v0.2.0/AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.0-windows-setup.exe) | 弹「Windows 已保护你的电脑」时点「更多信息」→「仍要运行」 | | Windows 10 / 11 · 免安装 | [AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.0-windows-portable.zip](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases/download/v0.2.0/AndroidAdCleaner-0.2.0-windows-portable.zip) | 解压后双击 `AndroidAdCleaner.exe` | 不知道 Mac 是哪种芯片：左上角苹果图标 → 关于本机，「芯片」写 Apple M 开头的选 Apple 芯片。所有版本：[Releases](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/releases)。用法：[docs/08-桌面客户端.md](docs/08-桌面客户端.md)。 | | | |---|---| |
**1 连接手机**：插线即认出手机，内置开启 USB 调试的图文教程 |
**2 检测**：型号、系统版本、机型脚本、快应用、广告组件 | |
**3 选择要关的**：营销通知按渠道勾选，服务类默认不勾 |
**4 执行**：进度条和实时日志 | |
**5 完成**：每一步的结果，最后提醒关闭开发者模式 |
**反馈**：自动附诊断信息，一键提交 GitHub Issue | --- - 不 root，不解锁，不刷机，系统更新不受影响。 - 只拨系统和 App 自带的开关。挂起广告包这一步要机主点头，一条命令可以还原。 - 搜索、负一屏卡片、应用商店的安装和更新、天气预警、快递提醒，这些功能保留。

改之前：OPPO 软件商店首页。轮播图、必备、必玩、福利标签，全是推广位。

--- ## 处理哪些东西 | 类别 | 例子 | 怎么处理 | |---|---|---| | 系统广告 | 个性化广告、广告跟踪（OAID）、智能推荐服务 | 系统设置里的开关 | | 热搜和资讯 | 下拉搜索的热榜、负一屏资讯、浏览器信息流 | 各 App 设置里的开关，浏览器切到简洁首页 | | 推广位 | 商店的轮播、开屏、悬浮活动、签到福利 | 商店「服务管理」里的开关 | | 营销推送 | 各 App 的「内容与营销」「活动优惠」通知 | 按渠道关，同一个 App 的订单、快递、更新通知保留 | | 广告组件 | `com.opos.ads`、`com.miui.systemAdSolution` 等 | `pm suspend` 挂起，要机主同意 | | 快应用 | 广告里一点就跳进去的「免安装小程序」 | `quickapp` 检测，`quickapp off` 关闭，见 [docs/07-快应用.md](docs/07-快应用.md) | ## 不做的事 - 不卸载、不停用系统应用（`pm uninstall`、`pm disable-user` 都不用）。 - 不改 system 分区，不装模块。 - 不替你同意任何 App 的用户协议。遇到协议页，点「取消」或「以后再说」。 - 不截账号页和手机号页。 --- ## 三种用法

> 用法一要先在手机上打开开发者模式和 USB 调试，带截图的教程：[docs/00-打开开发者模式.md](docs/00-打开开发者模式.md)。 | 用法 | 适合谁 | 要准备什么 | 文档 | |---|---|---|---| | **一：AI 智能体替你跑** | 有电脑，想省事 | 电脑、数据线、一个能执行命令的 AI 工具 | [docs/02-用AI智能体.md](docs/02-用AI智能体.md) | | **二：聊天 AI 带你点** | 只有手机 | DeepSeek、豆包、ChatGPT 任意一个 | [docs/03-用聊天AI.md](docs/03-用聊天AI.md) | | **三：照清单手动关** | 想自己掌握每一步 | 只要手机 | [docs/清单/](docs/清单/) | | **四：桌面客户端** | 不想敲命令 | Mac（Apple / Intel 芯片）或 Windows 10/11、数据线 | [下载](#下载桌面客户端) · [说明](docs/08-桌面客户端.md) | 用法一的开场白，复制给 AI： ```text 请克隆 https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner ，读仓库里的 AGENTS.md， 然后帮我给连着电脑的这台手机去广告。每一步改之前告诉我要改什么。 ``` --- ## 实测过的机型 **机型脚本**：一台机型的自动操作步骤，记着「打开哪个 App、点哪几个字进设置页、关哪几个开关、留哪几个」。电脑照着它在手机上点，几分钟做完。设置页因型号和系统版本而不同，所以每个机型一份。 | 品牌 | 机型（型号） | 系统 | 机型脚本 | 手动清单 | 营销通知 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 荣耀 | PNM-AN10 | MagicOS 10 | ✅ 实测通过，重跑 4 分钟 | ✅ | ✅ 26 个渠道 | | OPPO | Find N6（PLP120） | ColorOS 16.0.9 | ⚠️ 路径实测，整段待验证 | ✅ | ✅ 30 个渠道 | | OPPO | Find X10 Pro Max（PMX110） | ColorOS 17 | — | ✅ | ✅ | | OPPO | Find X9 Ultra（PMA120） | ColorOS 16.0.10 | ❌ 页面和 N6 不同，待补 | 部分 | ✅ 27 个渠道 | | OPPO | Find N3 典藏版（PHN110） | ColorOS 16.0.5 | ❌ 待补 | 部分 | ✅ 27 个渠道 | | 小米 | 18 Pro Max（M154FF） | HyperOS 4 | ⚠️ 路径实测，整段待验证 | ✅ | ✅ | | vivo | X300 Ultra（V2547DA） | OriginOS 6 | — | ✅ | ✅ | - 营销通知和广告跟踪两项是通用的，任何安卓手机都能跑。 - 同一个品牌，系统小版本不同，设置页的名字和层级也会变。机型脚本按型号和系统版本存放，版本对不上时引擎会提示，找不到入口的步骤会跳过，不会乱点。 - 你的机型不在表里：照 [docs/04-给新机型写脚本.md](docs/04-给新机型写脚本.md) 做一份，欢迎提 PR。 --- ## 一次完整的流程

命令写法： ```bash pip3 install -r requirements.txt python3 tool/run.py devices # 看序列号、型号、有没有机型脚本 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> check # 只读检查 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> backup # 改动前快照 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> recipe # 跑机型脚本 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> chan-scan # 列营销通知渠道 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> chan-off backups/<型号>-<时间>/channels.tsv python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> quickapp # 检测快应用；quickapp off 关闭 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> finish # 收尾，提醒关闭开发者模式 python3 tool/run.py -s <序列号> dev-off --yes # 从电脑关闭开发者模式（最后一步，执行后断开） ```

营销通知按渠道关：天气的「内容与营销」关掉，天气预警保留。

--- ## 仓库结构 ```text AGENTS.md 给 AI 智能体读的操作规范 docs/ 00-打开开发者模式.md 带截图的分步教程 01-准备工作.md 装 adb、连电脑、无线调试 02-用AI智能体.md WorkBuddy、Claude Code、Codex、Trae、Cursor 03-用聊天AI.md DeepSeek、豆包、ChatGPT 04-给新机型写脚本.md 05-还原.md 06-常见问题.md 07-快应用.md 什么是快应用、怎么检测和关闭 08-桌面客户端.md Mac 客户端的用法、数据位置、打包 清单/ 各品牌的手动清单 prompts/ 复制给聊天 AI 的提示词 tool/ run.py 总入口 fast.py 读屏、找入口、拨开关的引擎（uiautomator2） chan_fast.py 营销通知渠道 explore.py 新机型探路（实验） gui/ 桌面客户端（pywebview 界面 + PyInstaller 打包） recipes/<品牌>-<型号>/recipe.py 各机型的机型脚本 images/ 文档配图 ``` ## 反馈 遇到问题、想要新功能、希望支持你的手机，到 [Issues](https://github.com/rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner/issues/new/choose) 提交，选对应的模板。 用桌面客户端的话，点左下角「反馈问题」：会自动附上客户端版本、手机型号、系统版本和最近的日志（序列号已替换，不含应用列表和通知内容），打开 GitHub 页面后点提交即可。提交需要 GitHub 账号。 ## 还原 见 [docs/05-还原.md](docs/05-还原.md)。挂起的包和通知渠道各一条命令；App 内的开关按清单路径手动打开。 ## 声明 本项目只调用 Android 系统和厂商 App 公开提供的设置项。各厂商的界面随系统更新变化，使用前请备份，结果以你的手机为准。使用本项目造成的任何问题由使用者自行承担。 许可证：MIT
